subject: DPA scoping: minimal-privilege inventory + annotated dataflow request
messages:
From: Ari Goldstein <ari.goldstein@healthops.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: HealthOps Legal <privacy@healthops.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: minimal-privilege inventory & annotated dataflow for DPA scoping

Hi Priya,

Hope you’re well. As part of our DPA scoping for the HealthOps integration (HO-3421) Legal needs a short package covering how Redwood handles PII and the least-privilege controls in production. Can you provide the following by EOD 2026-10-18?

- A single-row subprocessor inventory with location (country), function, and whether they have access to plaintext PII (csv is fine).
- An annotated dataflow diagram that shows where PII enters the system, how it’s tokenized/pseudonymized, key custody, and where logs/audits are retained (PDF preferred).
- A short statement on minimal-privilege/access segregation for inference pipelines (who can access token cache, model artifacts, and exported telemetry).
- If any cross-border subprocessors are involved, please flag them and the legal basis for transfer.
- Pointer to a recent sample of audit logs (redacted) that show privilege elevation events.

Attachments are fine if small; if you prefer a Drive link that works too. Let me know if anything needs clarification.

Thanks,
Ari
Ari Goldstein
Senior Counsel, HealthOps
(Attachment request: subprocessor inventory, annotated dataflow, audit sample)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ari Goldstein <ari.goldstein@healthops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: minimal-privilege inventory & annotated dataflow for DPA scoping

Hi Ari — thanks for the clear list. We can get you a consolidated package. Quick clarifying points so we scope correctly: 

- For "access to plaintext PII" do you want fields that can be re-identified (raw user text) or any derived identifiers? We’ll mark both but primary focus will be re-identifiable fields.
- Your note on "audit logs" — is a 48-hour tail of privilege-elevation events sufficient or do you need a longer window? We can produce a redacted 7-day sample if needed.

Planned owners: Jordan will produce the annotated dataflow and KMS custody map; Marissa will assemble the subprocessor inventory and transfer/legal basis notes; Karthik will pull an audit tail and a short minimal-privilege statement for the inference pipeline. I’ll consolidate into a single zip and upload to Drive.

Target for our first draft: 2026-10-13 EOD. Final package by 2026-10-18 if you need the formal sign-off artifacts.

If that timeline is tight for you, tell us which items to prioritize and we’ll bump them up.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
(Attachment stub: none yet)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ari Goldstein <ari.goldstein@healthops.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: minimal-privilege inventory & annotated dataflow for DPA scoping

On Mon, Oct 11, 2026 at 11:05 AM Priya Natarajan wrote:
> Planned owners: Jordan will produce the annotated dataflow and KMS custody map; Marissa will assemble the subprocessor inventory and transfer/legal basis notes; Karthik will pull an audit tail and a short minimal-privilege statement for the inference pipeline. I’ll consolidate into a single zip and upload to Drive.

Thanks — attaching the draft diagram for initial review. This is a production-focused diagram (sequence: ingest -> tokenization/proxy -> inference runtime -> post-process -> telemetry export). Key callouts in the PDF:

- PKM: Key material is stored in customer-dedicated KMS partitions; Redwood does not export keys to subprocessors.
- Token cache: in-GPU KV cache is ephemeral; persists only to encrypted object store for warm start scenarios and is rotated per session.
- Access boundary: model artifacts are served from an internal artifact registry that only infra-team service accounts can modify.

(Attachment: annotated-dataflow-v0.3-draft.pdf)

Jordan
Engineering Manager, Runtime & Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Ari Goldstein <ari.goldstein@healthops.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: HealthOps Legal <privacy@healthops.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: minimal-privilege inventory & annotated dataflow for DPA scoping

Priya/Jordan — this is helpful, thank you. Quick follow ups before you finalize: 

1) Cross-border subprocessors: in your inventory please explicitly flag any subprocessors that process data outside the US and include the lawful transfer mechanism (SCCs, adequacy, consent, other).
2) Tokenization: does Redwood ever persist raw tokens outside the customer project boundary for debug or analytics? If so, we need retention and access controls.
3) SOC2/ISO: is there a single public URL or shared drive where we can find the latest SOC2 Type II report and any relevant penetration test summaries?

If you can get answers to 2 and 3 in the first draft, we can proceed with legal scoping. 48-hour audit tail is fine for the preview — we’ll request longer windows if required.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Ari

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ari Goldstein <ari.goldstein@healthops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: minimal-privilege inventory & annotated dataflow for DPA scoping

Ari — attached is the consolidated package per your asks. Highlights and quick answers below: 

Attachments included (in Drive and zipped):
- annotated-dataflow-v1.pdf (finalized diagram with callouts for tokenization, KV cache lifecycle, enclave boundaries)
- subprocessor-inventory-20261013.csv (columns: name, function, country, access_plaintext_pii, transfer_mechanism)
- kms-key-custody-matrix.xlsx (columns: key_id, owner, HSM/KMS, exportable)
- sample-audit-tail.txt (redacted 48-hour privilege-elevation events)

Short answers to your follow-ups: 
- Cross-border subprocessors: flagged in the inventory with transfer_mechanism populated (SCCs for EU subprocessors; adequacy + SCC fallback for UK). See column "transfer_mechanism" in the CSV.
- Tokenization persistence: Redwood does not persist raw user tokens outside the customer project boundary for routine telemetry. We do persist encrypted token caches to object storage for session warm starts; those artifacts are encrypted-at-rest and keyed with project-scoped KMS keys. Access is restricted to infra service accounts; any decryption requires KMS permission which is audited.
- SOC2/ISO: public SOC2 Type II link: https://redwoodinference.com/compliance/soc2-type2 (credentials required for full report; we can provide the report under NDA/LOA). Pen test summary also available on that page (redacted).

Next steps: if HealthOps Legal wants a longer audit window or a deeper look at KMS access logs we can schedule a joint session with infra ops and legal. We can also provide an export of the subprocessor contract annexes under NDA.

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cDefG_example
HubSpot record: HO-3421

Thanks — please confirm receipt and any prioritization for follow-up items.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
(Attachments: annotated-dataflow-v1.pdf, subprocessor-inventory-20261013.csv, kms-key-custody-matrix.xlsx, sample-audit-tail.txt)
